routes.description: Establish that irreducible and purposive patterns are real features of the world, trace their ordered unity toward Logos, and show how Genesis, resurrection, worship, and communal meaning become intelligible within that account.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if pattern realism and purposive hierarchy support a transcendent unifying source, while the scriptural, resurrection, and social claims operate as connected manifestations or consequences of that Logos-centered ontology.

motionBridge.description: Connect objective, purposive patterns and their unifying hierarchy to God as Logos rather than leaving them as merely cognitive or pragmatic abstractions.

centralBridges.description: Establish that higher-order identities have irreducible properties, persistence, or causal constraint not exhausted by their material constituents.
Show that purposive organization, mind, and value scale beyond individual cognition and require or indicate a transcendent unifying source.
Explain how symbolic narration can refer truthfully to reality and how enduring personal pattern makes resurrection coherent within the Logos account.
Connect worship and shared sacred orientation to the formation and maintenance of individual and communal purposes.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Identify limits of descriptions that bracket meaning, purpose, observer dependence, or formal and final causation.
Relate inherited scriptural and ritual forms to the continuity of moral and communal organization.

routes.description: Explain patterns, values, religious insight, and social coordination through cognition, abstraction, material organization, and cultural transmission while separating their practical usefulness from claims about transcendent Logos or historical resurrection.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if bottom-up cognitive and social mechanisms account for the relevant patterns and meanings, and if symbolic or pragmatic value does not entail divine ontology, privileged historical claims, or supernatural events.

motionBridge.description: Show that cognition, pragmatic abstraction, and bottom-up social life explain the cited phenomena without requiring God as Logos.

centralBridges.description: Locate patterns and classifications in perceiver-dependent abstraction while explaining why they remain useful, constrained, and nonarbitrary.
Account for persistent wholes and collective action through constituents, arrangements, beliefs, desires, and functional roles without independent higher minds.
Separate the moral or analogical value of religious narratives from their divine, historical, and postmortem claims.
Prevent religious social cohesion or moral efficacy from independently establishing the truth of a supernatural ontology.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain species-specific abstraction and perception through a natural cognitive continuum compatible with scientific inquiry.
Explain shared values and religious resonance through interpersonal inheritance, cultural familiarity, and local social norms.

sections.title: Patterns, Higher-Order Wholes, and the Inference to Logos
sections.rationale: This issue contains the primary motion-level clash over whether unified patterns have irreducible, causally significant reality that points toward transcendent Logos or remain useful structures grounded in parts and cognition.

sections.title: Perception, Abstraction, and the Scope of Scientific Explanation
sections.rationale: This issue tests the rival accounts of how perceivers encounter structure, whether mind dependence supports theism, and whether evolutionary and scientific explanation can accommodate the observed relation between cognition and world.

sections.title: Genesis, Symbolic Truth, and Historical Reference
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether Genesis supplies truth-bearing purposive orientation and disciplined reference to reality, or whether its analogical value can be retained without accepting privileged divine or historical claims.

sections.title: Resurrection, Personal Identity, and Pattern Persistence
sections.rationale: This issue bears directly on whether continuity of identity beyond changing matter makes bodily resurrection coherent and religiously necessary, or whether pragmatic insight and structural abstraction leave the historical claim unsupported.

sections.title: Worship, Value Hierarchies, and Social Meaning
sections.rationale: This issue examines whether worship and sacred centers enact genuinely transcendent purposes that organize communal life, or whether moral formation, cohesion, and collective action admit bottom-up social explanations without implying supernatural truth.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: The world's nested patterns of unity, multiplicity, and purpose point analogically toward an ultimate unity in God.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Higher-order unities exercise downward constraint on their parts, so labeling them emergent does not adequately explain their ontological reality.

chunk-002:c002-1074-1106.proposition: Genesis 1 describes reality through meaningful evaluation and supplies orientation about human place and conduct that a mechanical account such as the Big Bang does not provide.

chunk-002:c002-1301-1380.proposition: Genesis uses disciplined analogical language to describe a real remembered event or transformation in human nature rather than either scientific reportage or arbitrary fiction.

chunk-002:c002-1646-1693.proposition: Resurrection becomes intelligible after establishing a loving transcendent unity, although resurrection is not itself a proof of God and scripture presents it as mysterious rather than readily measurable.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: The persistence of intelligent patterns beyond changing material components makes resurrection conceptually credible because identity is not exhausted by its current substrate.

chunk-004:c004-01.proposition: Because the world cannot be thought, represented, or conceived outside mind, mind is foundational to any account of existence and supports at least a movement toward theism.

chunk-004:c004-05.proposition: Worship of the loving, self-sacrificial origin of reality binds participants toward that ideal, just as celebrating war disposes a society toward warlike purposes.

chunk-004:c004-06.proposition: Secular dismantling of shared sacred centers has fragmented social life, leaving communities without common places, celebrations, or purposes that bind people together.

chunk-005:chunk-005-candidate-002.proposition: Combining biologically constrained human perception with the scientific observer's frame may reintroduce formal and final causes into an adequate account of reality.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: Religious texts can convey substantial moral and aesthetic value to an atheist reader without requiring belief in their divine authority or historical claims.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: The world's formal organization, even considered in its entirety, does not by itself establish a transcendent being possessing intelligence or will.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Shared values are inherited from other people and mediated through individual minds, with religious resonance shaped by cultural familiarity rather than requiring a transcendent source.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Patterns are practically useful but depend specifically on human cognition rather than existing as mind-independent or divinely grounded realities.

chunk-002:c002-1284-1295.proposition: Biblical analogical teaching may be valuable while its claims about what historically occurred remain a distinct and more difficult basis for belief.

chunk-002:c002-1459-1546.proposition: Unlike recurring Genesis analogies observable in ordinary life, bodily resurrection and continued personal experience after death make distinct historical or phenomenological claims requiring separate support.

chunk-002:c002-1565-1636.proposition: Life-guiding scriptural patterns can be affirmed as analogical truths without accepting that their singular figures existed historically or that promised postmortem phenomena occur.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: The persistence of entities such as cities can be explained through nonarbitrary functional and structural abstractions maintained by human minds, without independently existing patterns or God.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-10.proposition: Human abstraction differs in degree from cognition in tool-using animals, so species-specific ways of organizing the world are compatible with an atheist natural continuum.

chunk-004:c004-07.proposition: Even if Christianity produced superior social harmony, that practical result would remain defeasible evidence compatible with natural explanation and alternative coherent value systems, not proof of God.
